title: Thrombotic microangiopathy and hypertensive kidney disease

steps.tx: **Thrombotic microangiopathy** (TMA) is defined by the pathological triad of microvascular endothelial injury, microvascular thrombosis, and erythrocyte fragmentation producing microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA with schistocytes) and thrombocytopenia. The image is microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and vascular onion-skinning in TMA. Schistocytes plus a low platelet count are the bedside clue.

vis.caption: Endothelial swelling, microthrombi, and fragmented red cells in thrombotic microangiopathy (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is caused by severe deficiency of the von Willebrand factor-cleaving protease **ADAMTS13** (activity < 10%), mediated by acquired autoantibodies or congenital mutations (Upshaw-Schulman syndrome). One side is TTP (ADAMTS13 < 10%), and the other side is aHUS (ADAMTS13 > 10%).
steps.say: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is caused by severe deficiency of the von Willebrand factor-cleaving protease ADAMTS13 (activity less than 10%), mediated by acquired autoantibodies or congenital mutations (Upshaw-Schulman syndrome). One side is TTP (ADAMTS13 less than 10%), and the other side is aHUS (ADAMTS13 greater than 10%).

left.title: TTP (ADAMTS13 < 10%)
points: Treated with plasma exchange and caplacizumab

right.title: aHUS (ADAMTS13 > 10%)
points: Dominant severe renal failure and hypertension

steps.tx: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (**aHUS**) is driven by uncontrolled dysregulation of the alternative complement pathway, caused by loss-of-function mutations in regulatory proteins (CFH, CFI, CD46/MCP) or gain-of-function mutations in C3 or CFB. The paired value for Complement Factor H (CFH) is Loss-of-function mutation or anti-CFH.

steps.tx: **Eculizumab** and ravulizumab are recombinant humanized monoclonal antibodies that bind complement protein C5, blocking cleavage into C5a and terminal membrane attack complex (C5b-9) assembly, representing first-line targeted therapy for aHUS. The first step is Alternative complement pathway hyperactivation. The next step is Eculizumab or ravulizumab binds C5.

nodes.label: Blocks cleavage into anaphylatoxin C5a and C5b
Prevents assembly of C5b-9 membrane attack complex

steps.tx: **Caplacizumab** is an anti-von Willebrand factor humanized single-variable-domain antibody (nanobody) that inhibits the interaction between vWF multimer A1 domains and platelet glycoprotein Ib-IX-V, accelerating platelet count recovery in acute TTP. The image is endothelial receptor binding and microvascular injury in hemolytic uremic syndrome.

steps.tx: Malignant nephrosclerosis is characterized histopathologically by hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis ('**onion-skin**' intimal thickening) and fibrinoid necrosis of afferent arterioles and glomerular tufts, presenting with acute severe hypertensive encephalopathy and AKI. One side is Malignant Hypertension, and the other side is Benign Nephrosclerosis.

left.title: Malignant Hypertension
points: Acute oliguric renal failure and encephalopathy

right.title: Benign Nephrosclerosis
points: Slow indolent loss of renal function

steps.tx: Benign hypertensive nephrosclerosis features **hyaline arteriolosclerosis**, medial hypertrophy, subcapsular cortical scarring with a finely granular kidney surface, and ischemic wrinkling of the glomerular basement membrane. The paired value for Malignant hypertension is Hyperplastic onion-skinning and fibrinoid necrosis. The paired value for Benign nephrosclerosis is Hyaline arteriolosclerosis with luminal narrowing.

rows: Rapidly progressive renal failure in malignant phase
Slow, modest proteinuria and gradual eGFR decline

steps.tx: **Scleroderma renal crisis** (SRC) manifests with acute onset oliguric AKI, accelerated hypertension, and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, where urgent initiation of ACE inhibitors (captopril) is life-saving, whereas systemic corticosteroids increase SRC risk. The first step is Systemic sclerosis patient exposed to corticosteroids.
